title: MAB-Seq
scope: Illumina explanatory core MAB-seq schematic, including its upper untreated bisulfite control and lower M.SssI branch. MAB-seq is M.SssI methylase-assisted bisulfite sequencing. The five icons represent cytosine modification classes at corresponding positions, not a literal five-base genomic sequence. The target is DNA-borne 5fC plus 5caC; the final carrier is amplified DNA encoding their combined signal as T. Library construction internals are not drawn. A separate primary-paper extension records the locus-specific caMAB-seq implementation explicitly mentioned by the catalogue: M.SssI, then selective 5fC reduction, then bisulfite/PCR. Its extra route is not depicted in the Illumina image and is not merged with the MAB-seq route. RRMAB-seq is recognized only at the related abstract evidence level; applicability of individual diagram operations and its unshown representation-selection front end are not resolved here.

states.label: Amplified MAB-seq DNA: schematic C-C-C-T-T
features: At CpG positions, originally unmodified C, 5mC and 5hmC are represented by C; original 5fC and 5caC by T.
The sequenced carrier is amplified DNA with a base-identity record of the original genomic cytosine state; original chemical modifications are not individually read on that product.
The T signal measures 5fC and 5caC together and cannot distinguish them. Non-CpG unmodified C is not reliably protected.
Incomplete methylase protection produces background T; inefficient conversion of the targets can reduce their T signal.
The far-right generic DNA endpoint does not depict a physical merger of the two branches.

operations.description: Retain an untreated comparator route from the input DNA, with no M.SssI methylation on this route. This is the depicted branch assignment, not a chemical conversion.
operations.information_effect: Original cytosine modification classes are retained until bisulfite treatment.

operations.label: M.SssI
operations.description: Treat DNA with the CpG methyltransferase M.SssI: unmodified CpG cytosine becomes 5mC, creating the bisulfite protection that distinguishes this assay.
operations.mechanism: M.SssI catalyses CpG C methylation. It is a reagent/catalyst, not a sequenced material or a separate DNA product.
operations.information_effect: Protection makes original unmodified CpG C join original 5mC/5hmC in the eventual C class, while 5fC and 5caC remain convertible.

operations.label: Bisulfite treatment; PCR amplification (Control)
operations.description: Convert bisulfite-susceptible bases in untreated DNA and amplify the converted template, yielding the depicted T-C-C-T-T product.
operations.mechanism: Standard bisulfite converts C and 5fC to uracil and 5caC to 5caU; their products are represented as T after amplification/sequencing. 5mC and 5hmC yield C calls. The depicted two-line operation is kept as one block.
operations.information_effect: The product conflates unmodified C, 5fC and 5caC into the T class; sequence-position association is retained.

evidence.locator: Upper arrow through "Bisulfite treatment / PCR amplification" to T-C-C-T-T
[b00008], Results: Experimental strategy and validation of MAB-seq
evidence.quote: In standard BS-seq, C/5fC/5caC react with sodium bisulfite and are efficiently deaminated to uracil (C/5fC) or 5caU (5caC), both of which are sequenced as thymine (T), whereas 5mC and 5hmC are resistant to this chemical conversion and sequenced as C (Fig. 1a).

operations.label: Bisulfite treatment; PCR amplification (M.SssI branch)
operations.description: Convert the methylase-protected DNA and amplify the converted template, yielding the depicted C-C-C-T-T product.
operations.mechanism: Originally unmodified CpG C is protected as 5mC; 5fC and 5caC remain bisulfite susceptible and produce T-coded positions after PCR. Original 5mC and 5hmC produce C-coded positions.
operations.information_effect: At CpGs, the physical carrier is amplified DNA and its T calls provide a direct combined 5fC/5caC signal at corresponding genomic positions. MAB-seq alone does not resolve 5fC from 5caC, nor C from 5mC/5hmC. Incomplete protection and conversion limit quantitative interpretation; the untreated control is a comparator, not an obligatory subtraction step. The fraction of T among C/T reads at a CpG supports quantitative combined-target abundance, with reaction efficiency and protection background taken into account; it does not separately identify either oxidized base.

operations.label: NaBH4 reduction (caMAB-seq; primary-paper extension)
operations.description: As the distinct caMAB-seq alternative, reduce 5fC in M.SssI-treated DNA to 5hmC before bisulfite treatment. This operation is reported in the primary paper and is not drawn in the Illumina image.
operations.mechanism: Sodium borohydride selectively reduces 5fC to 5hmC. M.SssI methylation precedes this reduction in the inspected locus-specific implementation.
operations.information_effect: Original 5fC is moved into the bisulfite-resistant C-read class; original 5caC remains in the T-read class. The input is an alternative use of protected DNA, not a depicted physical split or mixing of branch products.

operations.label: Bisulfite treatment; PCR amplification (caMAB-seq; primary-paper extension)
operations.description: Bisulfite-convert the selectively reduced, methylase-treated DNA and amplify selected loci to obtain DNA in which only original 5caC gives T. This paper-supported locus-specific variant is separate from the diagrammed combined-target MAB-seq product.
operations.mechanism: Originally unmodified CpG C is protected as 5mC and original 5fC as reduced 5hmC; these and pre-existing 5mC/5hmC yield C calls. Original 5caC yields T.
operations.information_effect: The PCR amplicon sequence carries a position-specific 5caC signal. This is the inspected locus-specific Illumina implementation, not evidence that the supplied diagram itself includes selective reduction or a genome-wide caMAB-seq library.

method_scopes.rationale: The lower path is MAB-seq; the upper path is the untreated standard-bisulfite comparator. MAB-Seq and M.SssI methylase-assisted bisulfite sequencing are aliases in this depiction. TET oxidation and TDG/BER in the catalogue description explain biological generation/removal of the target and are not depicted assay operations. The catalogue mentions caMAB-seq separately; its selective chemistry is not shown in this image.

Description: MAB-seq and caMAB-seq distinction
evidence.quote: MAB-seq allows simultaneous and quantitative mapping of both 5fC and 5caC at base resolution. This method is complimentary to caMAB-seq, a method for direct 5caC mapping.

method_scopes.rationale: caMAB-seq is a distinct method variant, not an alias for the diagrammed combined 5fC/5caC assay. Its M.SssI-to-NaBH4-to-bisulfite/PCR order and 5caC-only T interpretation are supported by the full-text locus-specific implementation. Sharing the protected-DNA state represents the expressly reported common M.SssI pretreatment; the two downstream operations are alternative methods, not sequential steps of MAB-seq. The diagrammed untreated control is not asserted as a required caMAB-seq operation.

method_scopes.rationale: The related 2016 protocol abstract expressly names reduced-representation MAB-seq and its increased coverage of CpG-rich regions. Full text was not acquired. This establishes a related variant, but does not establish which depiction-specific steps or representation-selection interfaces apply to its implementation; no individual operation is assigned from resemblance or the shared method name. This unresolved applicability does not prevent extraction of the two Illumina branches or of the fully supported caMAB-seq extension.

unknowns.question: For RRMAB-seq, which of the diagrammed operations apply, and what selected DNA state enters them? The supplied abstract names the variant and its CpG-rich coverage goal but does not show its representation-selection interface or preparation order. The protocol full text and its workflow figure for PMID 27281647 would be needed to assign a complete variant architecture.
